programs.program: Master mention Audiovisuel, médias interactifs numériques, jeux — parcours Conception sonore (game/interactive sound design)
programs.institution: Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (Cnam) — École nationale du jeu et des médias interactifs numériques (Enjmin)
programs.institutionType: Grand établissement / EPSCP (public higher-education and research establishment) — Enjmin is one of the Cnam's écoles (EPN)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: the Cnam is a state EPSCP under the Ministry of Higher Education; the Cnam's own governing-board annex on differentiated fees lists ENJMIN among the internal schools (EPN) that deliver initial training and must apply the state 'Bienvenue en France' differentiated-fee policy, which only applies to public establishments. The award is a diplôme national de master delivered by the state.
programs.qualification: Diplôme national de master (DNM), 'Master Sciences, technologies, santé mention Audiovisuel, médias interactifs numériques, jeux, parcours Conception sonore'. Real second-cycle state degree, RNCP code 38202, accreditation stated as running to 31 August 2030. Supports a student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited diplôme national de master; RNCP 38202; accreditation stated to 31/08/2030.
programs.language: French for M1 (semesters 1–2). The official Cnam page states for semester 3: 'les enseignements de ce semestre se déroulent en langue anglaise' — i.e. M2 is taught in English. So the degree is bilingual FR then EN.
programs.languageRequirement: The official application page states international candidates must supply a B2-level French certificate. No English certificate is demanded on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED whether any English proof is required for the English-taught M2; ask scolarite Enjmin (contact via enjmin.cnam.fr).
programs.englishTest: None published on the official pages I opened. UNVERIFIED — ask Enjmin admissions.
programs.focus: Sound design and audio implementation for video games and interactive digital media; the only public French school wholly dedicated to video games.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound design and audio production for games and interactive media inside a multidisciplinary game-production master (the six tracks — conception sonore, conception visuelle, ergonomie UX, game design, management de projet, programmation — build games together). Track chosen at application. M2 delivered in English. Concrete module list not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED, request the maquette from the scolarité.
programs.entryRequirements: RNCP level 6 diploma (licence, licence pro, BUT, bachelor) or equivalent bac+3; or VES/VAPP validation (3+ years of professional/personal experience). For a foreign diploma the official page requires an ENIC-NARIC France 'attestation de comparabilité' at CEC level 6 or above, plus B2 French. Then a competitive concours: creative dossier → written exam → oral exam. His BSc Software Engineering satisfies the academic bar; the concours does not.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — no music degree, conservatoire training or prior audio employment is required; the official page says no specific prior educational path is required and explicitly welcomes candidates with personal project experience. In practice the creative dossier is where a non-portfolio candidate fails.
programs.portfolioSpec: Mandatory 'dossier créatif' answering a published brief — 'Cahier des charges et sujet du concours 2026' (PDF published on enjmin.cnam.fr, released with the call). Followed by a written exam and an oral. Exact sound-track brief contents: see that year's cahier des charges — the 2027 brief will be published when the call opens.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. Selection is: creative dossier, then a remote written exam, then an oral (remote or on site).
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Not detailed on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Enjmin is the national public game school with game-production studios in Angoulême.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the 2026 concours brief was released Friday 12 December 2025, 15:00. Expect the 2027 call around mid-December 2026 — which fits his October 2026–February 2027 window.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: dossier deadline Friday 23 January 2026, 12:00 UTC+1. Dossier results 5 March 2026; written exam 28 March 2026 (remote); orals 26–29 May 2026; final results 3 June 2026; M1 begins 7 September 2026. The equivalent 2027 calendar had not been published at the time of checking.
programs.tuitionEU: Not published on the pages I opened. The Cnam page links to a 'Tarifs' form rather than stating a figure — UNVERIFIED. The national master rate set by ministerial order is the reference; ask Enjmin scolarité.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. The Cnam's own governing-board annex states the differentiated fees are '2 770 € pour une Licence et de 3 770 € pour un Master, avec une majoration prévue à 3 879 € pour le Master à partir de la rentrée 2024-2025', that 'Le CNAM applique les frais d'inscription différenciés', and it names ENJMIN among the schools concerned. Critically, the same document records that only three schools (ESGT, INSEAC, EPN5) agreed to exempt — ENJMIN is NOT among them. So expect roughly 3 879 € per year, no institutional exemption. Confirm the 2027-2028 figure with Enjmin before applying.
programs.otherFees: CVEC (contribution vie étudiante et de campus) is payable in addition — amount not stated on the Cnam pages I opened, UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Roughly 3 900 € tuition per year plus CVEC plus living costs in Angoulême; the school does not publish a living-cost estimate — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None specific to this programme on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. General French-government routes (Eiffel, Campus France Tunisia) are already in the database and would have to be paired with it.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. It is a diplôme national de master at a public establishment. Note the official page's important procedural point: since 2025 international candidates apply DIRECTLY through the Cnam-Enjmin concours, not through Études en France; Études en France is used only afterwards, once admitted, to obtain the visa.
programs.recommendation: The single best thematic fit in this sweep for a software engineer who wants to work in sound — game audio sits exactly on the seam between his BSc and his ambition, and the official page genuinely does not require a music degree. Two hard cautions. (1) The gate is a creative dossier plus written and oral exams for a very small public school; with no portfolio today he must spend 2026 building game-audio work specifically against the published cahier des charges, which appears in December. (2) It is NOT a DJ/producer programme — it trains game sound designers. Also note the cost: unlike most French universities, the Cnam does not exempt non-EU students, so budget ~3 879 €/year rather than the ~255 € headline. Deadline discipline matters: the brief drops mid-December and closes ~23 January, so he must have the ENIC-NARIC attestation de comparabilité and a B2 French certificate in hand by November 2026.

Teaching is in French, which he has. The honest caveat is what it is: broadcast/AV and sound-systems engineering — room acoustics, PA design, signal chains — not music production, and it will not by itself make him a producer or DJ. Treat it as a fundable, visa-safe technical base with a strong regional cost profile, and build the music side privately alongside. Budget the real 3 950 €/year, not the 255 € headline, unless he secures an exemption or an Eiffel-type scholarship.

programs.program: International Master of Science in Acoustics (Master Acoustique)
programs.institution: École Centrale de Lyon, in partnership with INSA Lyon and ENTPE (Université de Lyon), supported by the CeLyA acoustics laboratory cluster
programs.institutionType: Three public grandes écoles d'ingénieurs (state engineering schools) delivering a joint national master
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: Centrale Lyon, INSA Lyon and ENTPE are all state engineering schools (EPSCP / public establishments under ministerial supervision); the programme's own application page applies the state differentiated fee for non-EU students, a public-sector mechanism.
programs.qualification: Master of Science in Acoustics — a French diplôme national de master delivered jointly by Centrale Lyon, INSA Lyon and ENTPE. Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit. RNCP number not shown on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.accreditationStatus: State master delivered by three accredited public engineering schools. Specific RNCP registration not displayed on the official pages — UNVERIFIED, ask the programme office.
programs.language: English. Centrale Lyon's official page states the programme is delivered in English; the programme site notes English and/or French courses are provided, with French/English language support in M1 so that M2 courses can be followed in either language.
programs.languageRequirement: English B2 for both M1 and M2 entry (official Centrale Lyon page). The application page requires an English certificate — TOEFL iBT, TOEIC, IELTS or Cambridge — unless English is the applicant's native language or he completed at least 3 years of education in English.
programs.englishTest: REQUIRED: TOEFL iBT, TOEIC, IELTS or Cambridge, at a level corresponding to B2. Exact minimum scores are not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED, ask the programme office. He has not sat one; this is the one certificate he must book.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (M1 + M2), 740 hours of in-person instruction across both years, plus a 4–12 week internship in M1 and a 22–26 week thesis placement in M2. Total ECTS not stated on the pages I opened (27 ECTS are attributable to M2 optional specialisation courses) — UNVERIFIED, though a French DNM is 120 ECTS.
programs.focus: Scientific and engineering acoustics, with M2 specialisation options including sound perception — the closest branch to audio/psychoacoustics.
programs.whatYouStudy: M1: fundamentals of mechanics, continuum physics and data/signal processing plus introductory acoustics. M2 specialisation choices published on the official programme site: aeroacoustics, building acoustics, vehicle acoustics, sound perception, ultrasounds, vibro-acoustics, fluid-structure interactions. Theoretical courses, numerical and experimental work, laboratory projects, and more than one semester of research training as an intern in a laboratory or in industry, in France or abroad.
programs.entryRequirements: M1 entry: a bachelor's degree in a scientific subject related to the master's themes, plus English B2. Selection is on dossier. Required documents (official application page): CV, motivation letter, passport/ID copy, ID photo, reference letter(s), transcripts, copy of last degree awarded, English language certificate.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — it is a physics/engineering master and expects no music background whatsoever. His BSc Software Engineering is a plausible 'scientific subject', though acoustics normally assumes stronger physics/mechanics than a pure software curriculum; the admissions committee judges relatedness on dossier. Worth writing to them first with his transcript.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. No creative portfolio is requested — selection is purely academic dossier. This is decisive for a candidate with no portfolio.
programs.facilities: Backed by the CeLyA (Centre Lyonnais d'Acoustique) laboratory cluster, with laboratory-based projects and research internships; the programme states close connections to industry across several fields.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — the official application page I opened does not publish a dated calendar. Secondary sources referenced an application deadline of 30/04/2026 with a committee reply on 29/05/2026 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date), but I could not confirm those dates on the institution's own page; ask the programme office directly. The official page does state that international students must follow the Études en France procedure in parallel with the online application — for a Tunisian national the Campus France Tunisie calendar will bind first, so treat autumn 2026 as the real start.
programs.tuitionEU: Not stated on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED (the national master rate applies; ask the school).
programs.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: 3 770 € stated for non-EU students on the programme's official application page (master-acoustics.ec-lyon.fr/application). Confirm the 2027-2028 figure — the national differentiated master rate was uplifted to 3 879 € from 2024-2025 and several institutions now publish 3 941–3 950 €, so this figure may be behind.
programs.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition — amount not published on the programme pages, UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~3 800–4 000 €/year tuition plus CVEC plus Lyon living costs (Lyon is France's second-most expensive student city). No official living-cost estimate on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: No scholarship information on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Ask about Centrale Lyon / Université de Lyon international scholarships and pair with Eiffel (already in the database; note Eiffel is nominated by the institution, so he would need Centrale Lyon to put him forward, which means contacting them by autumn 2026).
programs.visaEligible: Yes — public establishments, national master, and the programme explicitly instructs international applicants to run Études en France in parallel.
programs.recommendation: Realistically his most admissible option in France: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no French-language gate, and an entry rule written for science graduates. It is also the one where his software background is an asset rather than an oddity, and 'sound perception' plus signal processing is a legitimate on-ramp to audio DSP and immersive-audio work. Three honest caveats. (1) It is acoustics engineering — it will not train him as a producer or DJ; that ambition has to be pursued in parallel. (2) His curriculum is software, not mechanics/physics; he should email the programme office with his transcript in autumn 2026 before investing in an application. (3) He must book IELTS or TOEFL — this is the only programme in this batch that demands a certificate he does not yet have. Cost is the standard non-EU rate with no exemption published, so plan on paying, or get nominated for Eiffel early.

programs.program: Master mention Musicologie — parcours Création-Production en musiques actuelles (CPMA) (the faculty also lists the track under the name 'Écoute critique et production en musiques actuelles')
programs.institution: Université de Strasbourg, Faculté des arts, Département de musique
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: Université de Strasbourg is a state university; its own tuition page publishes the ministerially-set national rate (255 €) and the differentiated non-EU rate, and its exemption decisions are taken by an institutional committee — both public-sector mechanisms.
programs.qualification: Diplôme national de master, mention Musicologie. Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit. RNCP number not shown on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited diplôme national de master at a public university.
programs.language: French (stated explicitly on the official catalogue page). An English course is included in the curriculum but instruction is French.
programs.languageRequirement: French at C1 — listed as a mandatory prerequisite on the official catalogue page ('bonne maîtrise de l'expression et de la rédaction en français', C1). He is fluent in French, so this is one of the few programmes where his language profile is an advantage; but he should expect to have to evidence C1 with a DELF/DALF or TCF certificate for the visa file.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS, 724 total teaching hours, in-person only (no distance option). Ends with a dissertation articulated with a public recital/production of roughly 60 minutes.
programs.focus: Music production and studio technology in the service of creation, in popular/contemporary music (musiques actuelles) — the closest thing in this sweep to his stated goal of music production and electronic music.
programs.whatYouStudy: Named on the official faculty page: critical listening and technical ear training; composition and orchestration with digital audio workstations; sound recording, mixing and mastering; analogue synthesis; composition for audiovisual and video games; sound design and artistic direction; professional practice in music production, publishing and copyright. Project-based pedagogy with substantial autonomous work; a 120-hour internship. Named outcomes: sound engineer, music producer, composer for audiovisual/games, sound designer, artistic director.

Mandatory prerequisites listed: advanced DAW skills; strong practical musicianship; composition and/or production competence; knowledge of sound reinforcement, acoustics or popular-music instrumentation; knowledge of the contemporary music industry; C1 French; academic research and writing competence; and music-theory fundamentals (score reading, analysis, composition), history and aesthetics of popular music.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO, in practice. The official entry rule is a music licence or an equivalent foreign degree, and the published prerequisites include score reading, analysis and orchestration. A BSc Software Engineering with no conservatoire training and no portfolio does not meet the stated conditions. He could only argue equivalence, and would still have to demonstrate the musicianship prerequisites.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not explicitly published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Given the prerequisites, expect production work to be assessed; ask the programme director, Sébastien Lebray (lebray@unistra.fr).
programs.auditionSpec: Not published — UNVERIFIED. The degree concludes with a public recital of ~60 minutes, which indicates a performing/producing standard is expected at entry. Confirm with the department.
programs.facilities: Studio-based teaching (recording, mixing, mastering, analogue synthesis) at the Faculté des arts, 14 rue René Descartes, Campus Esplanade. Specific studio inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — no dated calendar on the pages I opened. Route: applications go through Mon Master (monmaster.gouv.fr), EXCEPT non-European candidates resident in a country covered by the Études en France procedure. Tunisia is an Études en France country, so he would apply through Campus France Tunisie / Études en France, not Mon Master — and that calendar opens in autumn.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — confirm with the Faculté des arts and with Campus France Tunisie for the Études en France campaign closing date for a September 2027 intake.

programs.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: 3 950 € at master level for non-EU (extracommunautaire) students, published on the University of Strasbourg's own tuition page (2025-2026). Strasbourg operates a Tuition Fee Exemption Committee through which international students may individually request exemption from the differentiated fees — the exemption rate and criteria are not stated on the page I opened (UNVERIFIED; ask the Service de la vie universitaire). A transitional exemption exists only for students already enrolled at Unistra in 2023/24 and 2024/25, which would not cover him.
programs.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition — amount not stated on the page I opened, UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~3 950 €/year plus CVEC plus Strasbourg living costs, unless the exemption committee reduces the fee to the national 255 €. No official living-cost figure — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None specific to this programme on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. The relevant lever is the Unistra Tuition Fee Exemption Committee plus the national Eiffel route already in the database.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — public university, national master; but note the applicant route for Tunisians is Études en France rather than Mon Master.
programs.recommendation: On content this is the best match in France for what he actually wants — mixing, mastering, analogue synthesis, DAW composition, music for games, and the business of production, in a real state master's degree at low national fees if he wins an exemption. On eligibility it is the worst match in this batch: the official entry rule is a music licence, and the published prerequisites (score reading, analysis, orchestration, existing production competence) describe someone with years of formal musical training. He has none. Do not build the plan around it. If he wants to keep it alive, the only route is (a) write to Sébastien Lebray in autumn 2026 asking whether a non-music bachelor with a strong production portfolio can be considered under 'diplôme étranger équivalent', and (b) spend 2026-27 producing enough finished, mixed and mastered work to make that argument. Realistically this is a 2028 target, not 2027.

programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz is a Land Rhineland-Palatinate state university; the HfM Mainz is one of its schools and the degree is issued under JGU's authority.
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.Mus.), 4 semesters — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree issued by a state university (with doctoral progression available through JGU). Germany's first sound-art composition master at a music college, running since winter semester 2009/10.
programs.accreditationStatus: State university programme under the Landeshochschulgesetz RLP, with published Eignungsprüfungsordnung and study regulations on download.uni-mainz.de. Programme seal/expiry not stated — UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
programs.languageRequirement: REMARKABLY LOW: the official JGU study-programme record demands only 'Nachweis hinreichender deutscher Sprachkenntnisse (vergleichbar Niveau A1-GERR)' — proof of German comparable to CEFR A1, provable by certificate OR by the interview conducted during the aptitude examination. A1 German is achievable in a few months. This is the lowest published German-language bar of any record in this sweep and makes the programme unusually reachable for a non-German-speaking applicant. Confirm in writing with the HfM Mainz admissions office, since it is atypical.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years). ECTS figure not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED (the Studien-/Prüfungsordnung on download.uni-mainz.de will state it; a German M.Mus. of this length is normally 120 ECTS). Additional published rule: applicants whose bachelor is not yet conferred at the application deadline need at least 135 ECTS.
programs.focus: Sound art composition with an emphasis on spatialising and intermedial compositional strategies, drawing together new music, ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION, sound art, audiovisual art, radiophonic art and Ars Acustica into one thematic unit.
programs.whatYouStudy: Advanced individual artistic-compositional research; collaboration with media and art institutions; spatial/multichannel work. Career destinations named by the school: independent artistic practice, media, radio, and museum sound design.
programs.entryRequirements: THE MOST OPEN DOOR IN THIS SWEEP. Three routes: (1) a bachelor in Music, (2) a bachelor in Art, or (3) — stated explicitly — an applicant who completed a DIFFERENT degree programme may be admitted if a high level of artistic ability is demonstrated in the aptitude examination. Route (3) is precisely his situation: a BSc Software Engineering with no music degree is not automatically excluded.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage Eignungsprüfung, and note it is NOT an instrumental audition: (1) pre-selection on submitted materials, after which shortlisted candidates are given a project theme and 6-12 weeks to prepare; (2) an aptitude CONVERSATION of 20-45 minutes in which the candidate presents the prepared project sketch and discusses artistic background, interests and expectations. No instrument, no performance, no conservatory technique is tested. For a candidate with no conservatory training this is a far more winnable format than a classical audition.
programs.portfolioSpec: Application must contain: CV; a written justification of the choice of programme; work samples (Arbeitsproben) relevant to the field; a description of planned artistic projects plus a project sketch in sound-art composition. This is a concrete, writable specification — his portfolio year should be built to produce exactly these four items.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly — the regulation admits candidates from unrelated degrees on demonstrated artistic aptitude. Combined with the A1 German bar, this is the most permissive formal profile of anything found.
programs.facilities: HfM Mainz studios; collaboration with media and art institutions in the Rhine-Main area.
programs.intakes: Start semester not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED (German M.Mus. programmes with an Eignungsprüfung are usually winter-semester entry).
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. The school's own guidance says applicants must inform themselves in good time at the admissions office, as procedures and deadlines vary. Ask the HfM Mainz Studienbüro directly — and ask early, because the pre-selection stage plus 6-12 weeks of project preparation means the real timeline starts months before the aptitude conversation.
programs.deadline: NOT PUBLISHED on the programme pages — UNVERIFIED. Ask the Hochschule für Musik Mainz admissions office (musik.uni-mainz.de contact) for the Eignungsprüfung registration deadline for the 2027 intake. Do not assume a July date; music-college aptitude deadlines are typically much earlier (often March-April).
programs.tuitionNonEU: IDENTICAL — no non-EU tuition rate at JGU Mainz.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution (Studierendenwerk + AStA + semester ticket): amount NOT confirmed on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; ask the JGU Studierendensekretariat. JGU semester contributions include a broad regional semester ticket.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0 + semester contribution (UNVERIFIED) + Mainz living costs (moderate; Rhine-Main is cheaper than Frankfurt itself) + blocked account for the visa.
programs.scholarships: None programme-specific published. DAAD artistic-field scholarships (already in the database) are the route for a Tunisian national. A Meisterschülerstudium/Konzertexamen exists as a post-master artistic track at JGU, not a funding source.
programs.englishTest: None — German-taught, and only A1 German demanded.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state M.Mus. from a state university.
programs.recommendation: The most surprising find of this slice and the one I would tell him to look at hardest among the artistic options. It is the only programme found where (a) an applicant from an unrelated degree is explicitly admissible on artistic aptitude, (b) only A1 German is demanded on paper, (c) the aptitude test is a project conversation rather than an instrumental audition, and (d) the entire cost is a semester contribution. The catch is that it is sound-art COMPOSITION — spatial, intermedial, radiophonic — and not dance-music production; he must want that. Two things to do this year: get the exact Eignungsprüfung deadline and the ECTS/Studienordnung from the Studienbüro, and build a real project sketch, because everything turns on that one document. Second official source: https://www.studium.uni-mainz.de/studienwahl/studienangebot/klangkunst-komposition-mmus/

programs.institution: Hochschule Mittweida — University of Applied Sciences, Fakultät Medien (taught at the MediaTechSpace in Leipzig)
programs.city: Leipzig (teaching site); institution seated in Mittweida, Saxony
programs.institutionType: Fachhochschule / University of Applied Sciences (state), Free State of Saxony
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Hochschule Mittweida is a state UAS of the Free State of Saxony under the Sächsisches Hochschulgesetz; the official programme page states there are no tuition fees, which is the state-institution signature.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.), 120 ECTS — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. BUT see visaEligible: the delivery mode, not the degree, is the problem.
programs.accreditationStatus: State programme; study documents (Studien- und Prüfungsordnungen) are published on me.hs-mittweida.de. Programme seal/expiry UNVERIFIED — check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
programs.language: GERMAN. The official page states lectures and other teaching formats are offered in German.
programs.languageRequirement: Not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. A German-taught M.A. at a Saxon UAS normally requires DSH-2 / TestDaF 4x4. Ask the Fakultät Medien.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, PART-TIME alongside employment ('berufsbegleitend'), delivered as online coursework plus regular in-person sessions in Leipzig scheduled at off-peak times. Credit rule: 300 ECTS total are required for the degree — 180 from the bachelor + 90 from the master + 30 from professional practice or a pre-master project.
programs.focus: Media production craft: camera, SOUND (Ton), lighting, directing and editing. The faculty's facilities include sound studios, radio rooms and an acoustics lab. Audio is one component of an audiovisual-production degree, not the whole of it.
programs.whatYouStudy: Practice-heavy production training built on the Faculty of Media's long-standing media-training tradition, combining online modules with block attendance in Leipzig.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed first university degree with at least 180 ECTS, PLUS at least one year of professional experience (which in exceptional cases may be acquired during the programme). Enrolment is guaranteed on submission of the required documents — there is no competitive selection. His BSc meets the 180 ECTS bar; the one year of professional experience is the gate, and he has none in audio or media.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree required. But professional experience is required, which he lacks.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated — UNVERIFIED. A part-time online/block format normally assumes the student has their own working setup.
programs.facilities: MediaTechSpace Leipzig (next to the main railway station); Faculty of Media sound studios, radio rooms, acoustics laboratory, print workshop.
programs.deadline: NOT published on the English programme page — UNVERIFIED. Ask the Fakultät Medien student office.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fees (stated on the official page) — unusual for a berufsbegleitend master, and worth confirming that no separate Weiterbildungsentgelt applies.
programs.tuitionNonEU: No separate non-EU rate is published; the page states no tuition fees. UNVERIFIED whether any part-time/continuing-education charge applies to external students — ask before assuming EUR 0.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution amount UNVERIFIED. Travel/accommodation for the Leipzig attendance blocks is on the student.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Nominally very low on tuition, but unusable as a primary migration route — see the visa point.
programs.visaEligible: DOUBTFUL — TREAT AS NO. This is a part-time, employment-accompanying (berufsbegleitend) programme delivered largely online with block sessions. German student residence permits under §16b AufenthG are built around full-time, in-person degree study; part-time/distance formats are routinely refused or granted only where the applicant already holds another residence title. The official page says nothing about visa sponsorship. He should NOT plan a Tunisian student-visa application around this programme without written confirmation from the Ausländerbehörde Leipzig and the university's international office.
programs.recommendation: Reported mainly as a WARNING record. On paper it looks attractive — public, no tuition, 180-ECTS entry, guaranteed enrolment, real sound training. In practice it fails for him on two independent grounds: it requires a year of professional experience he does not have, and its part-time/berufsbegleitend format is a poor and probably invalid basis for a first German student visa. Do not spend application effort here for September 2027.

programs.institution: Hochschule der Bildenden Künste Saar (HBKsaar — Saar University of Fine Arts)
programs.institutionType: Staatliche Kunsthochschule (state university of fine arts), Saarland
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. HBKsaar is the state university of fine arts of the Saarland, described on its own pages as a state art college with a focus on the combination of art and technology.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.), 60 ECTS — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree, but note it is a SHORT master: the official master overview gives roughly 1 year (max 2 years) and 60 credit points, which is why it demands a 240-ECTS first degree.
programs.accreditationStatus: State art college programme. Programme seal/expiry not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de. Two other HBKsaar masters (Kuratieren/Ausstellungswesen and Museumspädagogik) are listed as SUSPENDED from WS 2026/27, which shows the portfolio is actively changing — re-check that Media Art & Design is still admitting before applying.
programs.language: Not stated on the official programme or master-overview pages — UNVERIFIED. HBKsaar teaches predominantly in GERMAN; the International Office page for this subject is written in English but describes the undergraduate course. Ask the International Office (Sabine Rauber, s.rauber@hbksaar.de, +49 681 92652-115) or mad@hbksaar.de which language the master is actually delivered in, and what certificate is demanded.
programs.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask s.rauber@hbksaar.de. Assume German at DSH/TestDaF level until told otherwise.
programs.durationEcts: Approximately 2 semesters / 60 CP (maximum 4 semesters), per the official Masterstudiengänge overview.
programs.focus: Digital technologies and the development of an individual creative practice: documentary and animation film, interactive productions, internet applications, artistic installations, games, media spaces, photography, media art, and explicitly SOUND AND LIGHT ART WORKS. Sound is named as a medium of the programme, but this is a media-art degree, not an audio-engineering or music-production degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-based work on electronic, time-based and interactive productions, supervised by Profs. Burkhard Detzler, Sung-Hyung Cho and Eric Lanz, with access to extensive workshops (wood, printing, CNC/3D printing, metal) alongside media project spaces.
programs.entryRequirements: HARD GATE: open to graduates of academic or artistic BA programmes with AT LEAST 240 ECTS. A 180-ECTS Tunisian BSc does NOT meet this. HBKsaar states a transition/bridging programme is offered for applicants with fewer credits — the terms, length and cost of that bridge are NOT published and are the decisive unknown. UNVERIFIED; ask mad@hbksaar.de.
programs.auditionSpec: None (art college; selection is by portfolio/artistic aptitude rather than audition). Exact procedure UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOT PUBLISHED on the official pages — UNVERIFIED. An artistic portfolio will certainly be required at a Kunsthochschule; ask mad@hbksaar.de for the specification before building work to the wrong brief.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES for the music point (no music degree needed), but the 240-ECTS rule is a harder obstacle than the artistic one.
programs.facilities: Media project spaces with current hardware/software; wood, printing, CNC and 3D-printing and metal workshops.
programs.deadline: NOT PUBLISHED on the official master pages — UNVERIFIED. Ask the International Office. German art colleges typically close portfolio applications in spring for a winter start.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee published (Saarland state institution) — UNVERIFIED as an explicit statement.
programs.tuitionNonEU: No separate non-EU rate published — UNVERIFIED. Saarland does not levy non-EU tuition at state institutions, but get this in writing from the International Office rather than assuming.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — too many unpublished figures to estimate honestly.
programs.englishTest: UNVERIFIED — depends on the (unpublished) teaching language.
programs.visaEligible: Probably yes for the M.A. itself (full-time state degree), but a 60-ECTS one-year master gives a short residence window, and any preliminary bridging year would need its own residence basis. Confirm with the International Office.
programs.recommendation: Reported for completeness of the Saarland — it is the only sound-touching master I could verify in that state — but it is a THIN record by design: HBKsaar publishes almost nothing about language, deadlines, portfolio or fees for its masters, and that opacity is itself the finding. The 240-ECTS entry rule likely excludes him outright unless the unpublished transition programme is generous. Low priority. If he wants to test it, one email to s.rauber@hbksaar.de asking four questions (language, portfolio spec, deadline, and the terms of the transition programme for a 180-ECTS holder) settles it. Programme description source: https://www.hbksaar.de/studiengaenge/media-art-design

programs.institution: Hochschule für Musik, Theater und Medien Hannover (HMTMH), Institut für Journalistik und Kommunikationsforschung (IJK)
programs.institutionType: Staatliche Hochschule für Musik, Theater und Medien (state university of music, drama and media), Lower Saxony — with university status and doctoral rights
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. HMTMH is a state institution of the Land Niedersachsen; the IJK is its media-research institute. Degrees are issued as university (Universitätsabschluss) master's degrees.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.), described by the IJK as a university-level master's degree (Universitätsabschluss Master of Arts). A real second-cycle degree with doctoral progression at HMTMH.
programs.accreditationStatus: State programme in Lower Saxony. Programme seal/expiry not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
programs.language: GERMAN (the programme's own materials and teaching are German; an English information page exists but the degree is delivered in German).
programs.languageRequirement: Not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. Expect DSH-2 / TestDaF 4x4. Ask the IJK (ijk@ijk.hmtm-hannover.de).
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters. ECTS not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED (normally 120). Only 17 places are awarded per year — a genuinely small, competitive cohort.
programs.focus: The intersection of communication science, musicology and media management. Named research foci: digital-media trends in MUSIC PRODUCTION AND MARKETING and their audiences; development of new offerings; strategies of pioneers and entrepreneurs in the media and music industry. Described by HMTMH as unique in Germany.
programs.whatYouStudy: Seven modules including three research projects, advanced methods training, strategic management, an individual profiling module, and a master thesis with defence. It is a RESEARCH and MANAGEMENT degree — there is no studio craft in it.
programs.entryRequirements: Normally a bachelor in communication science / media studies or in musicology; graduates of music-related artistic-academic programmes may also apply. A BSc Software Engineering is not among the named backgrounds — he would be applying against the grain into a 17-place cohort. Selection procedure not detailed on the pages read — UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Ambiguous — no music degree is required, but the named entry backgrounds are communication/media science and musicology, neither of which he holds. Ask the IJK whether a computing background with documented music-industry engagement is considered.
programs.facilities: IJK research facilities; HMTMH media and music infrastructure in Hannover.
programs.deadline: NOT published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. Ask ijk@ijk.hmtm-hannover.de.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition (Lower Saxony abolished tuition fees).
programs.tuitionNonEU: No separate non-EU rate is published; Lower Saxony charges no non-EU tuition at state institutions. Semester contribution only. Exact figure UNVERIFIED.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution amount UNVERIFIED — ask the HMTMH Immatrikulationsamt.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0 + semester contribution (UNVERIFIED) + Hannover living costs + blocked account.
programs.recommendation: Included to cover Lower Saxony and because it is a distinct HMTMH degree not previously in the database, but it is a POOR fit for his stated goal: it studies the music industry rather than teaching him to make records, it is taught in German, and it hands out only 17 places a year to applicants from communication science and musicology. Consider it only if his ambition shifts from producing to the business/research side. Institutional overview source: https://www.hmtm-hannover.de/de/bewerbung/studienangebote/medien-und-musik-ma/
